title: Discover a BMC and its capabilities
why: A single standard entry point reveals the management features available on an unfamiliar server.
outcome: Print the Redfish version and advertised service links before building automation.
requires: A Redfish service root; optional services vary by controller.
body:
root = rf.root
show(fields(root, 'RedfishVersion', 'UUID', 'Vendor', 'Product'))
show({key: value for key, value in root.items()
      if isinstance(value, dict) and '@odata.id' in value})

title: Populate a hardware asset register
why: The BMC exposes model and serial identity even before an operating system is installed.
outcome: Produce a CMDB-ready record with manufacturer, model, serial number and system UUID.
requires: ComputerSystem inventory; choose BMC_SYSTEM_ID when several systems exist.
body:
system = rf.system()
show(fields(system, 'Id', 'Manufacturer', 'Model', 'SerialNumber',
            'UUID', 'AssetTag', 'HostName', 'BiosVersion'))

title: Plan CPU capacity before deployment
why: Processor inventory gives a consistent hardware view without installing an agent on every host.
outcome: List sockets, processor models, core counts and threads for placement planning.
requires: The system must advertise a Processors collection.
body:
processors = rf.members(rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Processors'))
show([fields(p, 'Socket', 'Model', 'ProcessorType', 'TotalCores',
             'TotalThreads', 'MaxSpeedMHz') for p in processors])

title: Find empty or mismatched memory slots
why: Memory resources describe the physical DIMMs, which an OS capacity total cannot explain.
outcome: List DIMM locations, capacities, part numbers and operating speeds.
requires: A Memory collection with populated DIMM inventory.
body:
dimms = rf.members(rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Memory'))
show([fields(d, 'DeviceLocator', 'CapacityMiB', 'PartNumber',
             'MemoryDeviceType', 'OperatingSpeedMhz', 'Status') for d in dimms])

title: Inventory GPUs and PCIe accelerators
why: Chassis PCIe inventory identifies physical add-in devices independently of their host drivers.
outcome: List card models, serial numbers, firmware and interface details for accelerator fleets.
requires: Chassis PCIeDevices; GPU detail may need Processor or vendor extensions.
body:
devices = rf.members(rf.follow(rf.chassis(), 'PCIeDevices'))
show([fields(d, 'Id', 'Manufacturer', 'Model', 'SerialNumber',
             'FirmwareVersion', 'PCIeInterface') for d in devices])

title: Audit physical network adapters
why: A hardware inventory can distinguish installed NIC models from the interfaces currently visible to an OS.
outcome: Export NIC model, serial number and controller details for compatibility checks.
requires: Chassis NetworkAdapters collection.
body:
adapters = rf.members(rf.follow(rf.chassis(), 'NetworkAdapters'))
show([fields(a, 'Id', 'Model', 'Manufacturer', 'SerialNumber',
             'Controllers', 'Status') for a in adapters])

title: Inventory physical disks before installation
why: Storage links reveal the actual drives available to a bare-metal provisioning workflow.
outcome: List drive serial numbers, media types, protocols and capacities across controllers.
requires: System Storage with advertised Drives links.

title: Build a firmware inventory
why: UpdateService collects firmware identities in one place instead of requiring separate tools per component.
outcome: List installed firmware versions and whether each component is updateable.
requires: UpdateService FirmwareInventory.
body:
updates = rf.follow(rf.root, 'UpdateService')
items = rf.members(rf.follow(updates, 'FirmwareInventory'))
show([fields(i, 'Id', 'Name', 'Version', 'SoftwareId', 'Updateable') for i in items])

title: Map hosts to management controllers
why: Standard topology links connect a server to the controller that manages it, avoiding guessed host-to-BMC mappings.
outcome: Print each system identity and its advertised ManagedBy relationships.
requires: ComputerSystem Links.ManagedBy populated by the service.

title: Locate equipment within a rack
why: Chassis location metadata helps technicians connect a software incident to the physical machine.
outcome: Read chassis type, asset tag and available rack/placement information.
requires: Chassis Location metadata; operators may need to populate it first.
body:
for chassis in rf.members(rf.follow(rf.root, 'Chassis')):
    show(fields(chassis, 'Id', 'ChassisType', 'AssetTag', 'Location', 'SerialNumber'))

title: Screen servers for hardware health issues
why: An out-of-band health rollup is useful when the host is down or its monitoring agent is unreachable.
outcome: Print per-system health rollups and identify non-OK or unavailable status.
requires: ComputerSystem Status.HealthRollup or Status.Health.
body:
for system in rf.members(rf.follow(rf.root, 'Systems')):
    status = system.get('Status', {})
    health = status.get('HealthRollup') or status.get('Health')
    show({'system': system.get('Id'), 'health': health,
          'needs_review': health != 'OK', 'status': status})

title: Detect overheating before a shutdown
why: BMC temperature sensors keep working independently of application monitoring.
outcome: Compare valid Celsius readings with each sensor’s advertised upper critical threshold.
requires: Modern Sensors with Temperature readings in Cel; legacy devices may expose Thermal instead.
body:
for sensor in rf.sensors('Temperature'):
    reading = sensor.get('Reading')
    critical = sensor.get('Thresholds', {}).get('UpperCritical', {}).get('Reading')
    if sensor.get('ReadingUnits') == 'Cel' and isinstance(reading, (int, float)):
        show({'sensor': sensor.get('Name'), 'celsius': reading,
              'critical_threshold': critical,
              'over_threshold': reading >= critical if isinstance(critical, (int, float)) else None})

title: Identify stopped or degraded cooling fans
why: Hardware fan readings expose cooling failures even when the operating system has no fan driver.
outcome: List rotational readings with their units and status; a zero reading needs context because some fans intentionally stop.
requires: Rotational Sensors with Reading, ReadingUnits and Status.

title: Check power-supply redundancy
why: The chassis power subsystem reveals lost redundancy before the remaining supply fails.
outcome: Read redundancy groups and the health of each advertised power supply.
requires: Modern PowerSubsystem with PowerSupplies and PowerSupplyRedundancy.
body:
power = rf.follow(rf.chassis(), 'PowerSubsystem')
show({'redundancy': power.get('PowerSupplyRedundancy')})
show([fields(p, 'Id', 'Model', 'LineInputStatus', 'Status')
      for p in rf.members(rf.follow(power, 'PowerSupplies'))])

title: Pinpoint an unhealthy DIMM
why: A per-DIMM health record identifies the physical slot to replace instead of reporting only a generic memory error.
outcome: Print DIMM status alongside its locator and serial number.
requires: Memory collection and per-module Status; detailed error counts require Metrics support.
body:
for dimm in rf.members(rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Memory')):
    show(fields(dimm, 'Id', 'DeviceLocator', 'SerialNumber', 'Status'))

title: Spot drives predicted to fail
why: The BMC can expose controller-reported drive health before a drive disappears from the host.
outcome: List failure prediction and remaining media life; missing values remain unknown.
requires: Drive.FailurePredicted and optionally PredictedMediaLifeLeftPercent.

title: Investigate processor throttling
why: Hardware throttle causes help explain slower work that ordinary CPU utilization alone cannot.
outcome: Read operating speed, throttle state and reported causes for each processor.
requires: Recent Processor schema with Throttled and ThrottleCauses; these fields are optional.

title: Detect a downgraded PCIe link
why: PCIe link metadata can reveal a card running below its expected lane width or generation.
outcome: Show current and maximum PCIe interface details for comparison with the hardware design.
requires: PCIeDevice.PCIeInterface populated by the BMC.

title: Triage hardware faults from event history
why: Persistent BMC logs preserve hardware faults across host crashes and OS reinstallations.
outcome: Read log entries with severity, creation time and message identifiers.
requires: Manager LogServices with Entries; logs may also be linked from Systems or Chassis.

title: Detect a chassis intrusion
why: A chassis-open sensor provides a physical security signal beyond software authentication logs.
outcome: Print the advertised intrusion sensor state and its rearm policy.
requires: Chassis.PhysicalSecurity; a physical intrusion sensor must be installed.
body:
show({'chassis': rf.chassis().get('Id'),
      'physical_security': rf.chassis().get('PhysicalSecurity')})

title: Start a powered-off server
why: The BMC remains reachable when the main host is off, making remote startup possible.
outcome: Request host power-on and then re-read PowerState.
requires: ComputerSystem.Reset must advertise the requested ResetType; execution needs power privileges.
body:
system = rf.system()
show(rf.action(system, 'ComputerSystem.Reset', {'ResetType': 'On'}))
# Re-read after an appropriate wait when executing on real hardware.
show(fields(rf.get(system), 'PowerState', 'BootProgress', 'LastResetTime'))

title: Shut down gracefully for maintenance
why: A standard reset action lets an automation request an orderly host shutdown.
outcome: Ask the host to shut down; acceptance does not guarantee the OS has finished.
requires: ComputerSystem.Reset must advertise the requested ResetType; execution needs power privileges.
body:
system = rf.system()
show(rf.action(system, 'ComputerSystem.Reset', {'ResetType': 'GracefulShutdown'}))
# Re-read after an appropriate wait when executing on real hardware.
show(fields(rf.get(system), 'PowerState', 'BootProgress', 'LastResetTime'))

title: Power off an unresponsive host
why: The independent management path can recover a server whose OS no longer responds.
outcome: Request a forced power-off; this interrupts workloads and can lose unsaved data.
requires: ComputerSystem.Reset must advertise the requested ResetType; execution needs power privileges.
body:
system = rf.system()
show(rf.action(system, 'ComputerSystem.Reset', {'ResetType': 'ForceOff'}))
# Re-read after an appropriate wait when executing on real hardware.
show(fields(rf.get(system), 'PowerState', 'BootProgress', 'LastResetTime'))

title: Restart after a configuration change
why: A discovered reset action makes reboot orchestration consistent across supported servers.
outcome: Request a graceful restart and follow subsequent power/boot progress.
requires: ComputerSystem.Reset must advertise the requested ResetType; execution needs power privileges.
body:
system = rf.system()
show(rf.action(system, 'ComputerSystem.Reset', {'ResetType': 'GracefulRestart'}))
# Re-read after an appropriate wait when executing on real hardware.
show(fields(rf.get(system), 'PowerState', 'BootProgress', 'LastResetTime'))

title: Restore the desired state after a power outage
why: PowerRestorePolicy lets a bare-metal fleet express how hosts should behave when AC power returns.
outcome: Preview a policy change to restore the host’s last power state.
requires: Writable ComputerSystem.PowerRestorePolicy and support for LastState.
body:
system = rf.system()
show({'current_policy': system.get('PowerRestorePolicy')})
show(rf.patch(system, {'PowerRestorePolicy': 'LastState'}))

title: Cap a server’s power budget
why: Hardware power controls can enforce a rack budget without relying on each application to cooperate.
outcome: Preview a modern power-limit set point in watts, respecting advertised bounds.
requires: Writable EnvironmentMetrics.PowerLimitWatts excerpt; older services may use legacy PowerControl.

title: Measure instantaneous server power
why: BMC power sensors measure the physical system rather than estimating consumption from CPU utilization.
outcome: Read power sensors with units, timestamps and physical context.
requires: Sensors with ReadingType Power; only compare measurements with compatible units.
body:
for sensor in rf.sensors('Power'):
    show(fields(sensor, 'Id', 'Reading', 'ReadingUnits', 'ReadingTime', 'PhysicalContext'))

title: Track cumulative energy use
why: A hardware energy counter supports consumption reports without installing host software.
outcome: Read EnergykWh/EnergyJoules excerpts; use differences over time and handle counter resets.
requires: EnvironmentMetrics energy readings supported by the equipment.
body:
environment = rf.follow(rf.chassis(), 'EnvironmentMetrics')
show(fields(environment, 'EnergykWh', 'EnergyJoules'))
# Persist timestamped readings externally; subtract successive values only
# when the same counter has not reset. Watts and kWh are different quantities.

title: Assess power-supply conversion efficiency
why: Input and output power measurements help locate inefficient or overloaded supplies.
outcome: Estimate output/input efficiency only when both readings are present and input is positive.
requires: PowerSupply.Metrics with InputPowerWatts and OutputPowerWatts excerpts.
body:
power = rf.follow(rf.chassis(), 'PowerSubsystem')
for supply in rf.members(rf.follow(power, 'PowerSupplies')):
    metrics = rf.follow(supply, 'Metrics')
    incoming = (metrics.get('InputPowerWatts') or {}).get('Reading')
    outgoing = (metrics.get('OutputPowerWatts') or {}).get('Reading')
    efficiency = (100 * outgoing / incoming
                  if isinstance(incoming, (int, float)) and incoming > 0
                  and isinstance(outgoing, (int, float)) else None)
    show({'supply': supply.get('Id'), 'estimated_efficiency_percent': efficiency})

title: Choose a hardware power/performance policy
why: A platform power mode can align hardware behavior with a fleet’s energy or performance goals.
outcome: Preview PowerSaving mode where the system supports that writable policy.
requires: ComputerSystem.PowerMode and platform support for PowerSaving; effects vary by platform.
body:
system = rf.system()
if 'PowerMode' not in system:
    raise CapabilityError('PowerMode is not advertised')
show({'current_mode': system['PowerMode']})
show(rf.patch(system, {'PowerMode': 'PowerSaving'}))

title: Provision a server through one-time PXE boot
why: A one-time boot override starts bare-metal provisioning while preserving the usual disk boot policy.
outcome: Preview PXE as the next boot source; provisioning services and a separate restart are still required.
requires: ComputerSystem Boot supports Pxe and Once; a working PXE network is required.
body:
show(rf.boot('Pxe'))
# This selects the next boot; it does not reboot or install an OS by itself.

title: Boot an installer over UEFI HTTP
why: Redfish can point compatible firmware at an HTTP boot image for remote provisioning.
outcome: Preview a one-time UEFI HTTP boot URI and target.
requires: Boot target UefiHttp and writable HttpBootUri; firmware and network must support HTTP boot.
body:
show(rf.boot('UefiHttp', HttpBootUri=required('BOOT_IMAGE_URI')))
# Use a trusted boot image and the platform’s supported HTTP/HTTPS configuration.

title: Boot from an attached installer ISO
why: A remote CD override makes virtual-media installation possible without a technician inserting a disk.
outcome: Preview a one-time CD boot; attach media first and restart separately.
requires: ComputerSystem Boot supports Cd and virtual media is already attached.
body:
show(rf.boot('Cd'))
# Attach the ISO using case 039, then request a restart in a maintenance window.

title: Explain the server’s available boot options
why: Standard UEFI boot-option resources reveal which named devices firmware can actually start.
outcome: List boot option references, display names and UEFI paths.
requires: ComputerSystem Boot.BootOptions collection.
body:
boot = rf.system().get('Boot', {})
options = rf.members(rf.follow(boot, 'BootOptions'))
show([fields(o, 'BootOptionReference', 'DisplayName', 'UefiDevicePath',
             'BootOptionEnabled') for o in options])

title: Standardize the persistent boot order
why: Firmware boot ordering can be staged consistently across a bare-metal fleet.
outcome: Validate a requested list against discovered BootOptionReference values and preview the change.
requires: Writable BootOrder and BootOptions; a reboot may be needed to apply pending settings.
body:
system = rf.system()
options = rf.members(rf.follow(system.get('Boot', {}), 'BootOptions'))
known = {o.get('BootOptionReference') for o in options}
order = json.loads(required('BOOT_ORDER_JSON'))
if not isinstance(order, list) or len(order) != len(set(order)) or not set(order) <= known:
    raise ValueError('Use a unique JSON list of advertised boot references')
target = rf.settings(system) if system.get('@Redfish.Settings') else system
show(rf.patch(target, {'Boot': {'BootOrder': order}}))

title: Audit BIOS settings for configuration drift
why: The BMC exposes firmware attributes before and after an OS installation.
outcome: Print current BIOS attributes and the registry name used to interpret their allowed values.
requires: System Bios link; attribute names and values are vendor-specific.
body:
bios = rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Bios')
show(fields(bios, 'AttributeRegistry', 'Attributes'))
# Compare with a versioned baseline for this exact server model/BIOS version.

title: Stage model-specific BIOS settings
why: The Settings model separates proposed firmware changes from currently active settings.
outcome: Preview a change to the advertised pending BIOS resource; reboot separately to apply it.
requires: Bios @Redfish.Settings; validate desired values with the advertised AttributeRegistry first.
body:
bios = rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Bios')
desired = json.loads(required('BIOS_ATTRIBUTES_JSON'))
if not isinstance(desired, dict) or not desired or not set(desired) <= set(bios.get('Attributes', {})):
    raise ValueError('Choose attribute names advertised by this BIOS')
# AttributeRegistry defines vendor-specific value types and dependencies.
show(rf.patch(rf.settings(bios), {'Attributes': desired}))

title: Reset BIOS configuration to defaults
why: A discovered BIOS reset action supports repeatable recovery from a bad firmware configuration.
outcome: Preview the ResetBios action; consult pending-state information and reboot requirements afterward.
requires: Advertised Bios.ResetBios action; defaults can change boot and device settings.
body:
bios = rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Bios')
show(rf.action(bios, 'Bios.ResetBios', {}))
show(fields(rf.get(bios), 'ResetBiosToDefaultsPending', '@Redfish.Settings'))

title: Attach virtual installation or rescue media
why: The BMC can present a remote image as a local disk even when the host OS is absent.
outcome: Preview an InsertMedia action with a read-only ISO URL.
requires: Manager VirtualMedia with InsertMedia; set MEDIA_ID when more than one slot exists.

title: Eject installation media after provisioning
why: Removing virtual media avoids accidentally booting an old installer during a later restart.
outcome: Preview EjectMedia on the selected advertised virtual-media slot.
requires: VirtualMedia.EjectMedia action.
body:
media = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'VirtualMedia')), 'MEDIA_ID')
show(rf.action(media, 'VirtualMedia.EjectMedia', {}))

title: Check firmware against an approved baseline
why: One inventory API can feed compliance checks for BMC, BIOS and supported device firmware.
outcome: Report version matches, mismatches and components missing from the expected inventory.
requires: FirmwareInventory; FIRMWARE_BASELINE_JSON maps exact inventory IDs to approved versions.

title: Update firmware through a standard action
why: SimpleUpdate gives an advertised management path for installing a supported firmware image.
outcome: Preview the firmware request; an executed update may return 202 and a task Location.
requires: UpdateService.SimpleUpdate; image compatibility, privileges and reboot rules are platform-specific.

title: Track an asynchronous maintenance task
why: Task resources make long-running work observable instead of treating acceptance as completion.
outcome: Print task state, status, percentage and messages from the advertised Tasks service.
requires: ServiceRoot Tasks and a Task collection; select TASK_ID when several tasks exist.
body:
service = rf.follow(rf.root, 'Tasks')
task = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(service, 'Tasks')), 'TASK_ID')
show(fields(task, 'Id', 'TaskState', 'TaskStatus', 'PercentComplete',
            'StartTime', 'EndTime', 'Messages', 'TaskMonitor'))
# Poll at the server’s suggested Retry-After interval in a production workflow.

title: Restart an unhealthy BMC
why: Manager reset can recover the management controller independently from the host’s power action.
outcome: Preview a graceful BMC restart; management connectivity will temporarily disappear.
requires: Manager.Reset with GracefulRestart; do not confuse it with ComputerSystem.Reset.
body:
manager = rf.manager()
show(rf.action(manager, 'Manager.Reset', {'ResetType': 'GracefulRestart'}))

title: Light the correct chassis identification LED
why: A standard locator control helps a remote operator direct a technician to the right server.
outcome: Preview LocationIndicatorActive=true on the selected chassis.
requires: Writable Chassis.LocationIndicatorActive; older devices use IndicatorLED.
body:
chassis = rf.chassis()
if 'LocationIndicatorActive' not in chassis:
    raise CapabilityError('Modern locator LED control is not advertised')
show(rf.patch(chassis, {'LocationIndicatorActive': True}))

title: Check whether staged settings have applied
why: The Settings annotation links active configuration to pending configuration and application messages.
outcome: Display active/pending BIOS values and Settings messages instead of assuming PATCH changed the running firmware.
requires: Bios @Redfish.Settings.SettingsObject; messages and timestamps depend on the implementation.
body:
bios = rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Bios')
pending = rf.settings(bios)
show({'active': bios.get('Attributes'), 'pending': pending.get('Attributes'),
      'application_info': bios.get('@Redfish.Settings')})

title: Find firmware targets that can be updated
why: SoftwareInventory marks updateable components and their reset requirements before maintenance begins.
outcome: List eligible targets with reset requirements and stable resource links.
requires: FirmwareInventory Updateable and optional ResetRequiredOnUpdate.

title: Stage firmware for a later maintenance window
why: Compatible services can receive an image before activation, reducing work during a planned outage.
outcome: Preview SimpleUpdate with Stage=true; activation is a separate supported workflow.
requires: A recent SimpleUpdate action supporting Stage; check its ActionInfo or vendor documentation.

title: Verify the BMC clock before correlating events
why: Controller time determines the meaning of hardware event timestamps in incident timelines.
outcome: Read manager time, local offset and configured time source for clock-alignment checks.
requires: Manager time fields; compare with a trusted UTC reference outside this one-shot sample.
body: show(fields(rf.manager(), 'DateTime', 'DateTimeLocalOffset', 'DateTimeSource', 'TimeZoneName'))

title: Request a diagnostic support bundle
why: A discovered diagnostic action can gather controller evidence without needing a functional host OS.
outcome: Preview a manager diagnostic collection and inspect its resulting task or log entry when executed.
requires: LogService.CollectDiagnosticData supporting Manager; select LOG_SERVICE_ID.
body:
log = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'LogServices')), 'LOG_SERVICE_ID')
show(rf.action(log, 'LogService.CollectDiagnosticData', {'DiagnosticDataType': 'Manager'}))

title: Map storage controllers to their drives
why: Controller and drive relationships explain the physical topology behind an OS disk list.
outcome: Print controller capabilities, redundancy and the drives attached to a selected storage subsystem.
requires: System Storage; modern Controllers or legacy embedded StorageControllers.

title: Audit logical volumes and RAID levels
why: Volume resources describe controller-managed storage even before the OS recognizes it.
outcome: List volume capacity, RAID type, encryption and health.
requires: Storage Volumes collection.

title: Plan physical storage capacity
why: Physical drive capacity is useful for provisioning plans before filesystems or agents exist.
outcome: Total known drive capacity per controller, keeping missing capacity counts visible.
requires: Storage Drives and Drive.CapacityBytes; raw capacity is not usable RAID/filesystem capacity.
body:
for storage in rf.members(rf.follow(rf.system(), 'Storage')):
    capacities = [rf.get(d).get('CapacityBytes') for d in storage.get('Drives', [])]
    known = [c for c in capacities if isinstance(c, int)]
    show({'storage': storage.get('Id'), 'raw_bytes': sum(known),
          'drives_with_unknown_capacity': len(capacities) - len(known)})

title: Create a mirrored RAID volume
why: Supported controllers can provision resilient boot storage through their advertised volume collection.
outcome: Preview creation of a RAID1 volume using an operator-supplied, controller-compatible payload.
requires: An insertable Volumes collection and RAID1 support; VOLUME_CREATE_JSON must specify capacity/drive allocation as required by that controller.
body:
collection = rf.follow(rf.storage(), 'Volumes')
payload = json.loads(required('VOLUME_CREATE_JSON'))
# Example starting point: {"Name":"boot-mirror","RAIDType":"RAID1",
# "CapacityBytes":100000000000}. Drive selection/creation rules vary.
if not isinstance(payload, dict) or payload.get('RAIDType') != 'RAID1':
    raise ValueError('Supply a validated RAID1 creation payload for this controller')
show(rf.write('POST', collection, payload))

title: Initialize a newly provisioned volume
why: The advertised volume action provides a standard way to request controller-side initialization.
outcome: Preview a fast initialization; executing it can destroy existing data.
requires: Volume.Initialize supporting InitializeType Fast; select STORAGE_ID and VOLUME_ID.
body:
volume = rf.volume()
show(rf.action(volume, 'Volume.Initialize', {'InitializeType': 'Fast'}))
# This can erase data. Follow any returned Task and verify completion.

title: Follow a storage rebuild or background operation
why: Volume operations expose controller progress without depending on host management software.
outcome: Read operation names, percentages and volume health during maintenance.
requires: Volume.Operations populated by the controller for the operation in progress.
body:
volume = rf.volume()
show(fields(volume, 'Id', 'Status', 'Operations'))
# An empty Operations array means no advertised operation, not proof of all controller activity.

title: Monitor SSD wear and NVMe error counters
why: DriveMetrics can reveal endurance and media problems that capacity monitoring misses.
outcome: Read remaining media life, power-on hours, IO error counters and available NVMe SMART data.
requires: Drive Metrics support; individual counters are optional.
body:
metrics = rf.follow(rf.drive(), 'Metrics')
show(fields(metrics, 'PredictedMediaLifeLeftPercent', 'PowerOnHours',
            'UncorrectableIOReadErrorCount', 'UncorrectableIOWriteErrorCount', 'NVMeSMART'))

title: Identify the physical disk to replace
why: A drive locator LED connects a remote diagnosis to the exact disk bay.
outcome: Preview activating the selected drive’s location indicator.
requires: Writable Drive.LocationIndicatorActive; select DRIVE_ID.
body:
drive = rf.drive()
if 'LocationIndicatorActive' not in drive:
    raise CapabilityError('Modern drive locator control is not advertised')
show(rf.patch(drive, {'LocationIndicatorActive': True}))

title: Designate a global hot spare
why: Controller-backed hot-spare configuration supports recovery policies before a disk fails.
outcome: Preview assigning an eligible unused drive as a global hot spare.
requires: Writable Drive.HotspareType and a controller supporting Global; verify the drive is unused.
body:
drive = rf.drive()
show(fields(drive, 'Id', 'HotspareType', 'Status'))
show(rf.patch(drive, {'HotspareType': 'Global'}))

title: Sanitize a drive before reuse
why: An advertised hardware erase action can support a controlled decommissioning workflow.
outcome: Preview SecureErase with an explicitly chosen sanitization type; execution destroys data.
requires: Drive.SecureErase; SANITIZATION_TYPE must match the advertised allowable values and your disposal policy.

title: Audit management-network addresses
why: The controller’s interfaces describe the independent management path rather than the host data network.
outcome: Read BMC MAC addresses, IP configuration and link status.
requires: Manager EthernetInterfaces.

title: Inventory host-network identity for provisioning
why: MAC addresses discovered before installation can feed DHCP reservations and PXE provisioning.
outcome: List host Ethernet interface MAC addresses and advertised addresses.
requires: ComputerSystem EthernetInterfaces; visibility of host IP configuration varies.

title: Set a static BMC IPv4 address
why: Remote management-network configuration can prepare servers for a dedicated operations subnet.
outcome: Preview disabling DHCPv4 and setting a static address; execution can interrupt this connection.
requires: Writable manager EthernetInterface DHCPv4 and IPv4StaticAddresses; set INTERFACE_ID.
body:
interface = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'EthernetInterfaces')), 'INTERFACE_ID')
show(rf.patch(interface, {
    'DHCPv4': {'DHCPEnabled': False},
    'IPv4StaticAddresses': [{'Address': required('STATIC_IPV4'),
                             'SubnetMask': required('IPV4_NETMASK'),
                             'Gateway': required('IPV4_GATEWAY')}],
}))
# Plan alternate access before executing a management-network change.

title: Configure BMC DNS resolvers
why: A controller needs working DNS to reach named update, time and event destinations.
outcome: Preview a list of static DNS server addresses on the selected manager interface.
requires: Writable EthernetInterface.StaticNameServers; DHCP-supplied settings may take precedence.
body:
interface = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'EthernetInterfaces')), 'INTERFACE_ID')
servers = json.loads(required('DNS_SERVERS_JSON'))
if not isinstance(servers, list) or not all(isinstance(s, str) for s in servers):
    raise ValueError('DNS_SERVERS_JSON must be a JSON list of server addresses')
show(rf.patch(interface, {'StaticNameServers': servers}))

title: Inspect NIC physical link health
why: Port resources distinguish a cabling or negotiated-speed problem from an application networking issue.
outcome: List port link state, speed and health on each supported physical NIC.
requires: NetworkAdapter Ports collection; older services may expose NetworkPorts instead.

title: Check NIC virtualization capability
why: Hardware network-function metadata helps plan SR-IOV use before deploying a hypervisor.
outcome: Read virtual-function limits, enabled state and network function capabilities.
requires: NetworkInterface.NetworkDeviceFunctions and advertised SR-IOV-related fields.

title: Configure a NIC function’s VLAN
why: Supported adapters can stage hardware network-function settings before the host OS starts.
outcome: Preview enabling a VLAN on a selected network function; a reset may be required.
requires: Writable NetworkDeviceFunction Ethernet.VLAN; set NETWORK_INTERFACE_ID and FUNCTION_ID.
body:
interface = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(rf.system(), 'NetworkInterfaces')), 'NETWORK_INTERFACE_ID')
function = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(interface, 'NetworkDeviceFunctions')), 'FUNCTION_ID')
vlan = int(required('VLAN_ID'))
if not 1 <= vlan <= 4094:
    raise ValueError('Choose a valid VLAN ID (1–4094)')
target = rf.settings(function) if function.get('@Redfish.Settings') else function
show(rf.patch(target, {'Ethernet': {'VLAN': {'VLANEnable': True, 'VLANId': vlan}}}))

title: Audit iSCSI boot configuration
why: Out-of-band NIC function data can explain why a diskless host cannot find its boot target.
outcome: Read advertised iSCSI initiator and target configuration, with secrets redacted.
requires: NetworkDeviceFunction.iSCSIBoot on an adapter supporting iSCSI boot.

title: Map managed fabric switches and endpoints
why: Redfish fabric resources connect supported switches and endpoints through a common resource model.
outcome: Read each fabric’s type and its advertised switch/endpoint collections.
requires: ServiceRoot Fabrics; supported fabric management is separate from ordinary host networking.

title: Configure the BMC’s time servers
why: Consistent controller time improves the reliability of hardware incident timelines across a fleet.
outcome: Preview enabling NTP and setting its configured servers.
requires: Writable ManagerNetworkProtocol.NTP.NTPServers and ProtocolEnabled.
body:
protocols = rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'NetworkProtocol')
servers = json.loads(required('NTP_SERVERS_JSON'))
if not isinstance(servers, list) or not all(isinstance(s, str) for s in servers):
    raise ValueError('NTP_SERVERS_JSON must be a JSON list of server names or addresses')
show(rf.patch(protocols, {'NTP': {'ProtocolEnabled': True, 'NTPServers': servers}}))

title: Audit local management accounts
why: A central account inventory helps reveal stale access on many independent controllers.
outcome: List account names, roles, enabled state and password-change requirements.
requires: AccountService Accounts and permission to enumerate accounts.

title: Create a dedicated read-only observer account
why: A separate least-privilege identity lets telemetry collectors avoid sharing an administrator account.
outcome: Preview creation with the advertised ReadOnly role and an operator-supplied password.
requires: Insertable Accounts and a supported ReadOnly role; account-creation privileges are required.

title: Disable a departed user’s BMC account
why: Hardware management access needs its own offboarding because it persists outside the host OS.
outcome: Preview disabling a specifically selected account.
requires: Writable ManagerAccount.Enabled; set ACCOUNT_ID and preserve another administrative access path.
body:
service = rf.follow(rf.root, 'AccountService')
account = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(service, 'Accounts')), 'ACCOUNT_ID')
show({'selected_account': fields(account, 'Id', 'UserName', 'RoleId')})
show(rf.patch(account, {'Enabled': False}))

title: Rotate a local management password
why: A consistent account API can be integrated into a controlled credential-rotation workflow.
outcome: Preview a password update for a selected account without printing the new secret.
requires: Writable ManagerAccount.Password; some services require ChangePassword for self-service changes.
body:
service = rf.follow(rf.root, 'AccountService')
account = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(service, 'Accounts')), 'ACCOUNT_ID')
show(rf.patch(account, {'Password': required('NEW_ACCOUNT_PASSWORD')}))

title: Review the privileges behind each role
why: Role resources make controller access policies inspectable instead of relying only on role names.
outcome: List standard and OEM privileges for each advertised role.
requires: AccountService Roles and permission to read Role resources.

title: Standardize account lockout behavior
why: A controller-wide lockout policy reduces inconsistent protection across an operations fleet.
outcome: Preview a chosen failed-login threshold and lockout duration.
requires: Writable AccountService lockout properties; LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD and LOCKOUT_SECONDS follow your policy.
body:
service = rf.follow(rf.root, 'AccountService')
threshold, seconds = int(required('LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD')), int(required('LOCKOUT_SECONDS'))
if threshold < 1 or seconds < 1:
    raise ValueError('Choose positive lockout values supported by your BMC')
show(rf.patch(service, {'AccountLockoutThreshold': threshold, 'AccountLockoutDuration': seconds}))

title: Audit UEFI Secure Boot state
why: Firmware security state can be checked before trusting a newly provisioned host.
outcome: Read configured enablement, current-boot status and Secure Boot mode.
requires: ComputerSystem SecureBoot link; this is configuration evidence, not remote attestation.
body:
secure_boot = rf.follow(rf.system(), 'SecureBoot')
show(fields(secure_boot, 'SecureBootEnable', 'SecureBootCurrentBoot', 'SecureBootMode'))

title: Enable Secure Boot for a prepared platform
why: Redfish can stage a firmware security setting without manually entering every server’s setup screen.
outcome: Preview SecureBootEnable=true; compatible signed boot components and a reset may be required.
requires: Writable SecureBootEnable; validate signing keys and OS compatibility before execution.
body:
secure_boot = rf.follow(rf.system(), 'SecureBoot')
show(rf.patch(secure_boot, {'SecureBootEnable': True}))

title: Find expiring BMC HTTPS certificates
why: Certificate inventory allows management-plane TLS expiry to be monitored like other infrastructure.
outcome: List HTTPS certificate subjects, issuers and validity dates.
requires: Manager NetworkProtocol HTTPS.Certificates.
body:
protocols = rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'NetworkProtocol')
https = protocols.get('HTTPS', {})
for certificate in rf.members(rf.follow(https, 'Certificates')):
    show(fields(certificate, 'Id', 'Subject', 'Issuer', 'ValidNotBefore', 'ValidNotAfter'))

title: Replace a management HTTPS certificate
why: CertificateService provides a discoverable way to renew a controller’s management certificate.
outcome: Preview replacing a selected HTTPS certificate with a trusted PEM certificate.
requires: CertificateService.ReplaceCertificate; PEM must match the controller’s key/CSR and trust configuration.
body:
service = rf.follow(rf.root, 'CertificateService')
protocols = rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'NetworkProtocol')
certificate = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(protocols.get('HTTPS', {}), 'Certificates')), 'CERTIFICATE_ID')
pem = Path(required('CERTIFICATE_PEM_FILE')).read_text()
show(rf.action(service, 'CertificateService.ReplaceCertificate', {
    'CertificateUri': {'@odata.id': rf.path(certificate)},
    'CertificateType': 'PEM', 'CertificateString': pem,
}))

title: Assign an asset tag during fleet enrollment
why: A writable asset tag binds the physical chassis to an organization’s inventory identifier.
outcome: Preview assigning a chosen chassis asset tag.
requires: Writable Chassis.AssetTag; ASSET_TAG is your inventory identifier.
body:
chassis = rf.chassis()
show(rf.patch(chassis, {'AssetTag': required('ASSET_TAG')}))

title: Inventory Redfish-capable rack PDUs
why: PowerEquipment extends a common inventory approach to compatible rack power infrastructure.
outcome: List rack PDU model, serial number, capacity and location.
requires: A facility/PDU controller exposing PowerEquipment.RackPDUs; ordinary server BMCs may omit it.

title: Measure power at individual rack outlets
why: Outlet measurements help attribute physical power use to equipment connected to a compatible PDU.
outcome: Read per-outlet power, energy and electrical consumer labels.
requires: Redfish RackPDU Outlets and metered readings; set PDU_ID.
body:
equipment = rf.follow(rf.root, 'PowerEquipment')
pdu = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(equipment, 'RackPDUs')), 'PDU_ID')
for outlet in rf.members(rf.follow(pdu, 'Outlets')):
    show(fields(outlet, 'Id', 'PowerWatts', 'EnergykWh', 'ElectricalConsumerNames', 'PowerState'))

title: Find overloaded PDU branches
why: Circuit measurements reveal rack electrical constraints that no single server can see.
outcome: Read branch current, rated current, load percentage and breaker state.
requires: RackPDU Branches collection with Circuit measurements.
body:
equipment = rf.follow(rf.root, 'PowerEquipment')
pdu = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(equipment, 'RackPDUs')), 'PDU_ID')
for branch in rf.members(rf.follow(pdu, 'Branches')):
    show(fields(branch, 'Id', 'CurrentAmps', 'RatedCurrentAmps',
                'PowerLoadPercent', 'BreakerState', 'Status'))

title: Power-cycle a selected PDU outlet remotely
why: A switched PDU can recover equipment whose own management controller is unreachable.
outcome: Preview PowerCycle for a verified outlet; execution removes power from its connected equipment.
requires: Outlet.PowerControl supporting PowerCycle; confirm PDU_ID, OUTLET_ID and cabling ownership.
body:
equipment = rf.follow(rf.root, 'PowerEquipment')
pdu = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(equipment, 'RackPDUs')), 'PDU_ID')
outlet = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(pdu, 'Outlets')), 'OUTLET_ID')
show(fields(outlet, 'Id', 'ElectricalConsumerNames', 'UserLabel'))
show(rf.action(outlet, 'Outlet.PowerControl', {'PowerState': 'PowerCycle'}))

title: Inventory liquid-cooling distribution units
why: ThermalEquipment provides a hardware management model for compatible cooling infrastructure in dense racks.
outcome: List CDU capacity, coolant information and health.
requires: A cooling/facility controller exposing ThermalEquipment.CDUs.

title: Monitor coolant flow and heat removal
why: Coolant connector measurements help explain thermal problems in liquid-cooled infrastructure.
outcome: Read flow, temperatures, pressure difference and heat removed from advertised secondary connectors.
requires: CoolingUnit.SecondaryCoolantConnectors with measurements; set CDU_ID.
body:
equipment = rf.follow(rf.root, 'ThermalEquipment')
cdu = rf.choose(rf.members(rf.follow(equipment, 'CDUs')), 'CDU_ID')
for connector in rf.members(rf.follow(cdu, 'SecondaryCoolantConnectors')):
    show(fields(connector, 'Id', 'FlowLitersPerMinute', 'SupplyTemperatureCelsius',
                'ReturnTemperatureCelsius', 'DeltaPressurekPa', 'HeatRemovedkW', 'Status'))

title: Detect a leak in a liquid-cooled chassis
why: Physical leak detectors provide an urgent hardware signal outside the host application stack.
outcome: Read detector state, physical context and health for the selected chassis.
requires: Chassis LeakDetectors collection; earlier models may link through ThermalSubsystem.LeakDetection.

title: Watch rack intake temperature and humidity
why: Environmental measurements help connect room conditions to server thermal health.
outcome: Read advertised ambient temperature, humidity and dew-point excerpts.
requires: Chassis EnvironmentMetrics and appropriate environmental sensors; some equipment omits these readings.
body:
environment = rf.follow(rf.chassis(), 'EnvironmentMetrics')
show(fields(environment, 'AmbientTemperatureCelsius', 'HumidityPercent',
            'DewPointCelsius', 'DewPointProximityCelsius'))

title: Find field-replaceable assembly part numbers
why: Assembly inventory helps order the correct spare for a physical maintenance visit.
outcome: List assembly members, part numbers, spare part numbers and serial identities.
requires: Chassis Assembly with Assemblies array.
body:
assembly = rf.follow(rf.chassis(), 'Assembly')
show([fields(a, 'MemberId', 'Name', 'PartNumber', 'SparePartNumber',
             'SerialNumber', 'Version', 'Status') for a in assembly.get('Assemblies', [])])

title: Subscribe a hardware-event webhook
why: EventService pushes faults soon after they occur, reducing reliance on repeated log polling.
outcome: Preview a Redfish event subscription to an operator-controlled HTTPS receiver.
requires: EventService Subscriptions, callback reachability and receiver TLS trust; production receivers must validate and deduplicate events.

title: Export hardware fault history as OTel logs
why: Redfish supplies hardware evidence while the OTel SDK routes it into the same log system used by applications.
outcome: Export a one-shot set of BMC log entries with source time, severity and stable server identity.
requires: Manager LogServices plus the installed OTel SDK; continuous collectors must checkpoint/deduplicate entry IDs.
body:
with RecipeTelemetry(rf.system()) as telemetry:
    for log in rf.members(rf.follow(rf.manager(), 'LogServices')):
        for entry in rf.members(rf.follow(log, 'Entries')):
            telemetry.log(entry.get('Message', 'Hardware event'),
                          severity=entry.get('Severity', 'OK'), timestamp=entry.get('Created'),
                          attributes={'redfish.log.id': log.get('Id', ''),
                                      'redfish.entry.id': entry.get('Id', ''),
                                      'redfish.message_id': entry.get('MessageId', '')})
# Console by default; OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT sends HTTP/protobuf to a Collector.

title: Discover periodic hardware telemetry reports
why: Report definitions describe the measurements and schedules a controller can publish.
outcome: List report types, schedules, metric properties and report actions before choosing a collection strategy.
requires: TelemetryService.MetricReportDefinitions; support and minimum intervals vary.
body:
service = rf.follow(rf.root, 'TelemetryService')
show(fields(service, 'MinCollectionInterval', 'MaxReports'))
show([fields(d, 'Id', 'MetricReportDefinitionType', 'Schedule', 'MetricProperties',
             'Metrics', 'ReportActions', 'MetricReportDefinitionEnabled')
      for d in rf.members(rf.follow(service, 'MetricReportDefinitions'))])

title: Convert a MetricReport to OTel gauges
why: An adapter can translate BMC metric reports into observable measurements for a shared backend.
outcome: Export numeric current readings with explicitly supplied units; report timestamps are printed separately.
requires: TelemetryService.MetricReports; METRIC_UNITS_JSON maps MetricId to verified units from MetricDefinitions. Use current readings, not accumulated history.
imports:
import re
from redfish_lab.recipe_telemetry import RecipeTelemetry

title: Export temperature into an OTel dashboard
why: A Python adapter makes Redfish temperatures available to the same metrics backend that monitors software.
outcome: Export valid Celsius sensor readings as real OTel observable gauges.
requires: Temperature Sensors in Cel plus the OTel SDK; missing readings are skipped rather than replaced with zero.
body:
with RecipeTelemetry(rf.system()) as telemetry:
    for sensor in rf.sensors('Temperature'):
        reading = sensor.get('Reading')
        if sensor.get('ReadingUnits') == 'Cel' and isinstance(reading, (int, float)):
            telemetry.gauge('redfish.hardware.temperature', reading, 'Cel',
                            {'redfish.sensor.id': sensor.get('Id', '')})
            show(fields(sensor, 'Id', 'ReadingTime'))
# Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318 for the optional Collector.

title: Export physical power into OTel metrics
why: Redfish watt readings complement application throughput when evaluating energy use.
outcome: Export watt-valued power sensors as OTel gauges with stable host and sensor identities.
requires: Power Sensors in W; collection interval and freshness must suit the equipment.

title: Give hardware and application signals a shared identity
why: A system UUID or serial number can join hardware readings to the application running on that physical server.
outcome: Build an OTel Resource with stable host.id and a separate service instance identity.
requires: System UUID or SerialNumber; the application must use the same verified host.id mapping.
body:
resource = hardware_resource(rf.system(), service_name='hardware-observer')
show(dict(resource.attributes))
# Configure the application SDK with this same host.id (and its own service.name).
# Match by identity and time; hardware events do not automatically have request trace IDs.

title: Trace the latency of a hardware polling request
why: Instrumenting the adapter reveals slow or failing BMC reads in the observability pipeline itself.
outcome: Export a real span covering an actual HTTPS sensor read and its measured duration.
requires: Sensors plus the OTel SDK; this is an adapter request trace, not a trace emitted by Redfish.
imports:
import time
from redfish_lab.recipe_telemetry import RecipeTelemetry
body:
system = rf.system()
chassis = rf.chassis()
with RecipeTelemetry(system) as telemetry:
    with telemetry.tracer.start_as_current_span('redfish.poll.sensors') as span:
        started = time.perf_counter()
        sensors = rf.members(rf.follow(chassis, 'Sensors'))
        span.set_attribute('redfish.sensor.count', len(sensors))
        span.set_attribute('redfish.poll.duration_ms', (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
    show({'sensors_read': len(sensors)})

title: Alert when hardware telemetry is stale
why: A healthy-looking last value is misleading if a controller has stopped supplying fresh samples.
outcome: Compare source ReadingTime with current UTC and export warning logs for stale or unparseable samples.
requires: Sensors with timezone-qualified ReadingTime and synchronized clocks; SAMPLE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS sets the threshold.
imports:
import time
from redfish_lab.recipe_telemetry import RecipeTelemetry, source_timestamp
body:
limit = float(required('SAMPLE_MAX_AGE_SECONDS'))
if limit <= 0:
    raise ValueError('Choose a positive freshness limit')
with RecipeTelemetry(rf.system()) as telemetry:
    for sensor in rf.sensors():
        stamp = source_timestamp(sensor.get('ReadingTime'))
        age = (time.time_ns() - stamp) / 1e9 if stamp is not None else None
        if age is None or age > limit or age < -5:
            telemetry.log('Missing, stale or future hardware sample', severity='Warning',
                          attributes={'redfish.sensor.id': sensor.get('Id', ''),
                                      'redfish.sample.time': sensor.get('ReadingTime') or 'unknown'})

title: Correlate hardware heat with application request latency
why: Redfish supplies temperatures and OTel supplies measured application spans, allowing a backend to compare them by server and time.
outcome: Export hardware gauges and a span around a real instrumented work function under the same host identity.
requires: Temperature Sensors, OTel SDK and application instrumentation on the same mapped host; correlation alone does not prove causation.
body:
def application_work():
    # Run on the managed host; this is local work, not remote execution by Redfish.
    # Replace this measured demonstration with your actual application request.
    return sum(i * i for i in range(100_000))

with RecipeTelemetry(rf.system()) as telemetry:
    for sensor in rf.sensors('Temperature'):
        value = sensor.get('Reading')
        if sensor.get('ReadingUnits') == 'Cel' and isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            telemetry.gauge('redfish.hardware.temperature', value, 'Cel',
                            {'redfish.sensor.id': sensor.get('Id', '')})
    with telemetry.tracer.start_as_current_span('application.work'):
        result = application_work()
    show({'result': result, 'join': 'host.id + overlapping time window'})
# In production, instrument the application separately with its own service.name.
